answer.rationale: The mandate and expiring contract push toward the low-cost vendor (c2), which met cost targets with clean onboarding historically. But c2's record is silent on delivery reliability under tight capacity, which is the current critical risk (94% of committed volume, no buffer, 14-day deadline). I verify c2's original source to check for any omitted delivery-performance details before committing capital to a full switch. Given the no-buffer constraint, I'm treating this as a standard (not broad) rollout of the new primary vendor rather than an immediate full-volume cutover, and flagging that a second-source hedge (c3) may be warranted next cycle if delivery risk materializes. This preserves the cost mandate while not treating the switch as risk-free.
